newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ABSA FOLLOWS TREND WITH S.AFRICA PRIME CUT.
newsitem.headline: ABSA FOLLOWS TREND WITH S.AFRICA PRIME CUT.

text.p: South Africa's Amalgamated Banks of South Africa Ltd (Absa) said on Thursday it was reducing its prime overdraft rate to 19.25 percent from 19.50 while the home loan rate would go to 19.00 percent from 19.25, with effect from October 1.
Absa's decision follows similar 0.25 point reductions by First National Bank Holdings Ltd and Standard Bank Investment Corp Ltd .

Absa also said its rate cut reflected the government's decision to scrap the Financial Services Levy (FSL) and replace it with value added tax (VAT) on financial services from next month. FSL was first introduced by the South African government in 1991, when banks increased prime by 0.25 percent to recover the cost.
